tokens.source: orchestrator_usage (joint dispatch: engine fix + example re-attempt)

prompts.text: Lift the >31-hop routing ceiling: when a planned route exceeds the 5-bit hop field, split it at an intermediate cell and emit the relay program so the packet is forwarded with a fresh hop count. Reuse the existing broker/transmit machinery; preserve payload AND trigger semantics; never consume a cell already used by a block; report the relay area cost. Then use the lifted ceiling to finish the gru_classifier example.

notes: INFRASTRUCTURE (wave 7). The router already PLANNED relay cells for >31-hop routes but the build never programmed them, so the net was failed with 'relay programming is not yet emitted by the build'. Emitted it: build._relay_program (land -> MOVE [FACE] -> re-emit WRITE+JUMP with a fresh budget, the crossover land/flip/re-emit primitive specialised to one track -- no new cell program invented) + build._apply_relays (chained BACKWARD so each relay addresses the resolved entry of the next; the source is re-pointed at the first; the LAST relay reproduces the net's ORIGINAL dest/entry so the destination sees exactly what a hop-legal route would have delivered). bus_router._plan_relays is the SINGLE planner shared by the router, the build, the DRC hop_overflow check and the controller's add_route guard, so no gate can accept a long route another rejects; bus_router.relay_plan DERIVES the cells from the routed project (build-from-design), so hand-placed .kyt files get relays too. Cost is reported via ChipBuild.relay_cells/.relay_cost (~1 cell per 30 hops). VERIFIED ON CHIP, not merely built: a 52-hop egress (previously impossible -- @32 does not even assemble) routes/builds/runs bit-exact against a hop-legal short-route control, and a 96-hop route chains THREE relays (30/30/30/6) and still delivers, so relays compose and no practical ceiling remains beyond array area. Mutations proven to FAIL: relay omitted (pre-fix behaviour, zero output), stale hop count (word stranded), relay mis-faced off the corridor; plus hard rejection of a relay on a block cell / used chip-port cell / existing broker (INV-32, port_transit class). 15 new gates in placekyt/tests/test_relay_emit.py. Two test_drc.py cases asserted the OLD contract (>31 hops always an error) and now assert the new one including that an unrelayable long route is still named. Recorded as INV-36. NOTE: this did NOT unblock gru_classifier -- see __gru_classifier_example__ -- that example's wall is corridor congestion ('no bus path from source to the broker tap'), not hop count. INFRASTRUCTURE (INV-36): lifted the 31-hop routing ceiling. A WRITE/JUMP carries a 5-bit HOP_CNT so one emission reaches at most 31 hops (measured: @31 delivers, @32 raises). The ROUTER ALREADY PLANNED relay cells and then failed the net with 'relay programming is not yet emitted by the build' — the gap was almost entirely in the build's EMIT path, as hypothesized. Long routes now split into <=31-hop segments; the word lands on an intermediate plain routing cell whose relay program flips to the continuation face and re-emits payload AND trigger with a fresh budget (the CrossoverBlock land->flip->re-emit primitive specialised to one track; no new cell program invented). FOUR THINGS THAT HAD TO BE RIGHT: emit the JUMP as well as the WRITE (payload-only = a silent stream that never triggers); chain BACKWARD (each relay addresses the resolved entry of the next, source re-pointed last, final relay reproducing the net's original dest/entry); ONE shared planner (_plan_relays) used by router, build, DRC hop_overflow, and the controller's add_route guard — three gates independently enforced <=31 and would otherwise have disagreed; hard rejection on block/used-port/broker cells (INV-32). PROOF: a 52-hop egress routes, builds and runs BIT-EXACT against a hop-legal short-route control (the relay is transparent to data); a 96-hop route chains THREE relays (30/30/30/6) and still delivers, so relays compose and NO CEILING REMAINS beyond array area. Cost ~1 cell per 30 hops, reported via ChipBuild.relay_cells/.relay_cost. 17 gates. MUTATION-QUALITY LESSON: the builder's first 'wrong face' mutation LEAKED — not a relay bug but a lucky geometry forwarding the word back onto the corridor; fixed by mutating the face constant directly in loaded chip memory and choosing faces that genuinely leave the route. 'A mutation a geometry can repair is a weak mutation.'
